reread/gen: A language model writes one token at a time, and its K V cache, K and V for keys and values, keeps every earlier token's key and value, in every block.
reread/read: But each new token's queries read the whole cache, in every block, at every step: the longer the text, the more there is to keep, and to read again.
reread/shazeer: In 2019, Noam Shazeer, an author of Attention Is All You Need, showed that this reading is what limits the speed: chips compute far faster than they fetch numbers from memory.
reread/heads: The heads make the cache big. In multi-head attention, each of h query heads has its own key head and value head, so each token keeps h keys and h values per block.
reread/count: With h at eight, and each head sixty four numbers wide, that is two, times eight, times sixty four: one thousand and twenty four numbers per token, per block.
mqa/ask: Shazeer's question: each query head must look for something different, so the queries must differ. But must the keys and values?
mqa/mqa: His answer, multi-query attention, keeps all h query heads, but gives them one key head and one value head to share: many queries, one key and value.
mqa/small: Each token now keeps two, times one, times sixty four: a hundred and twenty eight numbers per block, h times fewer.
mqa/fast: In his tests, each new token came out more than ten times faster, with only a minor loss in quality.
groups/cost: One shared head can cost quality, though. In 2023, Joshua Ainslie and colleagues at Google Research found a middle way: grouped-query attention, or G Q A.
groups/group: Split the query heads into groups, and give each group one key head and one value head. Write g for the number of key-value heads: with g at two, each serves a group of four.
groups/attend: Each query head still makes its own scores and its own blend, reading its group's keys and values. Grouped queries: hence the name.
groups/shape: Stacked head first, for T tokens, the queries are eight, by T, by sixty four. The keys are only two, by T, by sixty four, and so are the values.
groups/shrink: The cache keeps two times g times sixty four: two hundred and fifty six numbers per token and block, four times fewer than multi-head: h over g.
groups/ends: So g sets the trade. At g equal to h, every query head has its own: plain multi-head attention. At g of one, it is multi-query.
groups/paper: In between, the paper found quality close to multi-head attention, at a speed close to multi-query.
model/p: Now a whole model: thirty two blocks, often called layers, each with h of eight, g of two, and heads sixty four wide.
model/all: Each layer keeps its own two hundred and fifty six numbers per token, so thirty two layers keep eight thousand one hundred and ninety two.
model/bytes: Each number takes two bytes of memory, so that is sixteen thousand three hundred and eighty four bytes per token.
model/kb: A kilobyte, or K B, is one thousand and twenty four bytes, so that is sixteen K B per token.
model/mha: With a key head and a value head for every query head, it would be four times as much: sixty four K B per token.
